notes:
PREREQUISITE FINDING (the actual result of this probe): resolve_duplicate cannot be exercised on its success path in project 379335744 (PR-2005) because no duplicate pair exists here in ANY state, not just not in `suggested`. get_dedupe_status returns {status:'NOT_ENABLED', message:'No dedupe job found for this project'} — the dedupe pipeline has never run for this project at all, which is stronger than 'pairs exist but got resolved already'. list_duplicates independently confirms an empty page ({duplicates:[], info:{count:0,total_pages:0}}), consistent with the NOT_ENABLED state (per that capability's own guidance, an empty listing is ambiguous between 'feature off' and 'ran and found nothing' — the status call resolves the ambiguity here in favor of 'feature off/never run'). Per list_duplicates's own guidance, 'there is no way to create a suggestion or trigger a scan through this API' — so this is not a payload problem, a permissions problem, or a timing problem; it is a hard structural block. No amount of retrying or rebuilding the payload fixes it, so per the campaign's own criterion this is UNVERIFIED, not BLOCKED (the index's declared contract is not shown to be wrong — it simply cannot be tested here) and not a guess.

DOES THIS UNBLOCK get_duplicate_source_test_case? No, and from the other direction than expected. That capability needs a `merged` pair; resolve_duplicate is plausibly the write that produces one, but only if a `suggested` pair exists to resolve first — and none does, anywhere in this project. Both reads (get_duplicate_source_test_case's need for a merged pair, and resolve_duplicate's need for a suggested pair) trace back to the SAME root blocker: dedupe has never run for PR-2005, so the pipeline that manufactures `suggested` pairs never fired. This is a prerequisite gap one level upstream of the previously-recorded finding, not a resolution of it. Whether a project WITH dedupe enabled and a real suggested pair would let resolve_duplicate create a merged pair (and thereby unblock the source-snapshot read) remains untested and untestable from here.

ERROR-CONTRACT CHECK (partial, does not require a real pair): a resolve attempt with an out-of-range duplicate_id (999999999) returned exactly the declared 404 shape, {errors:'Duplicate not found.'} (plural key, matching the description precisely) — this one corner of the contract is confirmed correct, for whatever that is worth against a synthetic id. This does NOT verify the 200 success path, the merge/archive body validation order, the 422 'Test case not found in duplicates' path, the 409 migration-pause path, or the 403 tc_delete-permission path — none of those could be reached without a real suggested pair.

DESTRUCTIVE-IN-EFFECT (self-reported by the index, NOT independently verified here): describeCapability's own guidance states plainly that `merge_action:'merge'` archives source_testcase_id (tags it 'Archived as Duplicate', posts a merge comment on the target, snapshots the source) and `merge_action:'archive'` archives archive_testcase_id outright — in both cases a test case is removed from active view as a side effect of a capability classed `write`, not `destructive`. If that self-report is accurate, this is exactly the pattern flagged for `unlink_test_runs_from_test_plan`: a non-destructive-classed write that produces a destructive-shaped effect (a case disappearing from folders/listings) and so is never intercepted by the runtime gate that blocks the whole destructive tier. I could NOT confirm this by observation — no live invocation reached the success path — so this is flagged as an open concern for the product team to confirm, not a verified finding. Recommend a follow-up probe once a project with dedupe enabled and an in-project probe-created suggested pair (never one touching __readonly__ 764093 / TC-54455 / TC-54456 / TC-54458 (1975349)) becomes available, verifying by reading BOTH cases back afterward (get_test_case + folder listing, not the write response, which the contract itself says is just {success:true} and echoes nothing about the affected cases).

RESOLVE vs DISCARD: resolve_duplicate takes duplicate_id in the BODY and posts to the collection path; discard_duplicate takes duplicate_id as a PATH segment on a distinct path. Discard is the 'not a duplicate' verdict — touches neither test case, just moves the pair to `discarded` (permanent, no un-discard) and needs only tc_write. Resolve is the 'yes, act on it' verdict — needs the heavier tc_delete permission, and always ends with the pair `merged` regardless of whether merge_action was 'merge' or 'archive' (the field name 'merge_action' is used for both, which is itself a naming overload worth flagging: an 'archive' action still sets the pair's terminal status to 'merged', not to some 'archived' pair-status). Error envelopes also differ: resolve uses `errors` (plural) on 404, discard uses `error` (singular) on 404 — one more instance of the inconsistent error-envelope drift already tracked (3/11 correct) across this surface.

ENTITLEMENT/other gates not exercised: the 403 tc_delete-permission gate and the 409 migration-pause gate were not (and could not be) triggered without a real pair.

ENV: live preprod, project 379335744 / PR-2005. Nothing was resolved, merged, archived, or otherwise mutated against any real test case — the one write call made targeted a nonexistent duplicate_id specifically so it would fail at the pair-lookup step, before any test-case id (real or otherwise) could be touched.
